FINDING_ID: VC_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: Authenticated continuity is not enforced across persistence boundaries. [verification_chain.py#L509](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L509) rebuilds a chain with no signer, and [verification_chain.py#L401](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L401) then defaults new records to `claimed_only`. [verification_chain.py#L588](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L588) verifies only records still marked `authenticated`, so a signed chain can silently continue with unsigned records and still pass `verify_chain(verifier)`. I reproduced this with a real Ed25519 keypair: first record authenticated, second `claimed_only`, overall verification still returned success.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Persist a chain-level authentication policy and enforce it on append. If any prior record is authenticated, require a signer for continuation unless an explicit, committed downgrade record is added and verification policy allows it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: [verification_chain.py#L463](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L463) is not a safe validity check for “record `n` in this chain”. It calls `_verify_single()` only for that index, and [verification_chain.py#L553](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L553) trusts the stored predecessor `chain_hash` without first verifying the predecessor record. I verified that corrupting record 0 makes `verify_chain()` fail while `verify_record(1)` still returns `(True, "OK")`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either make `verify_record()` verify the full prefix `0..index`, or rename and document it as a local self-consistency check that does not establish prefix integrity.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The CLI never performs authenticated verification, but presents success as if it did. [verification_chain.py#L655](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L655) and [verification_chain.py#L663](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L663) call verification with no `Verifier`, and [verification_chain.py#L733](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L733) exposes no signer/public-key options at all. So the public CLI can neither create signed records nor verify signatures, yet still reports “verified”.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add CLI support for signing and key resolution, or explicitly downgrade the CLI contract to “hash-only verification” and fail or warn when authenticated records are present but no verifier material is supplied.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: The public API leaks live mutable state across both input and output boundaries. [verification_chain.py#L376](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L376) stores caller-owned `payload`/`metadata` objects by reference; [verification_chain.py#L419](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L419), [verification_chain.py#L519](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L519), [verification_chain.py#L523](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L523), and [verification_chain.py#L528](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L528) return the stored dicts or shallow copies only. I verified that mutating the original payload, the returned record, `head()`, or `records[0]` rewrites the sealed chain in place.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Deep-copy or freeze `payload` and `metadata` on append, and return deep copies or immutable views from all read APIs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: Epoch verification accepts impossible states. [verification_chain.py#L447](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L447) returns early for an empty record list, so bogus epochs are never checked at all. Separately, [verification_chain.py#L603](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L603) does not reject negative `record_count`, and [verification_chain.py#L611](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L611) then uses Python slicing semantics, so `record_count = -1` verifies against “all but the last record”. I reproduced both cases.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Always verify epochs even when the chain is empty, require `record_count` to be an integer in `[0, len(records)]`, and reject impossible epoch metadata before hashing.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: Verification enforces hash consistency but not the persisted record schema. [verification_chain.py#L571](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L571) special-cases only `storage_mode == "full_payload"` and otherwise accepts any other mode silently. I verified that a persisted `hash_only` record can be rewritten to `storage_mode = "banana"` with an injected `payload`, hashes recomputed, and [verification_chain.py#L439](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L439) still reports the chain valid.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit schema validation during load/verify: allowed `storage_mode` enum only, `payload` required for `full_payload`, forbidden for `hash_only`, and analogous validation for signature fields and epoch structure.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: Inclusion-proof verification does not prove the claimed leaf position. [verification_chain.py#L480](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L480) emits an `index`, but [verification_chain.py#L487](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L487) ignores it completely. I verified that changing `proof["index"]` to `999` does not affect `verify_inclusion_proof()` at all. So the API proves only “this leaf hashes to this root along this path”, not “this leaf was at the claimed index”.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `index` from the proof object, or move to full RFC 9162-style verification with enforced `index` and `tree_size` inputs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
